valuetypes.[val1, ...]: Multiple values between a set of square brackets denotes possible types/values for a single field.
valuetypes.\"...\": Anything between double quotes is a string literal. This is mostly used in conjunction with the above square brackets syntax.
valuetypes.list(...): Lists are a series of values that can repeat on a single line, separated by commas/semicolons. Example of list(int, bool): "1,false;2,true"
valuetypes.repeatable(...): Repeatable keys can be used for multiple lines. An example of this would be an item with multiple "bonus" lines.
valuetypes.bool: a string value of  true  or  false
valuetypes.item_id: specifies an integer item identifer (greater than 0)
valuetypes.power_id: specifies an integer power identifer (greater than 0)
valuetypes.icon_id: specifies an integer icon identifer (greater than or equal to 0)
valuetypes.point: defined as:  int, int : X, Y
valuetypes.rectangle: defined as:  int, int, int, int : X, Y, Width, Height
valuetypes.filename: a string path to a file relative to the base of the mod directory (e.g. "animations/hero.txt")
valuetypes.color: defined as:  int, int, int : Red, Green, Blue
valuetypes.predefined_string: same as a string, but uses a value defined elsewhere
valuetypes.direction: defined as:  ["N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW", int] . If defined as an integer, the value must be between 0-7 inclusive, mapping to  ["SW", "W", "NW", "N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S"]  respectively.
valuetypes.duration: durations can be specified in seconds and milliseconds with integer suffix s, ms (eg. 20s, 20000ms)
valuetypes.label: defined as:  "hidden"   or   int, int, ["left", "right", "center"], ["top", "center", "bottom"], string : X, Y, Justify, Vertical Align, Font style . The font style can be any style defined in engine/font_settings.txt.
valuetypes.loot: defined as:  filename   or   ["currency", item_id], ["fixed", float], int, int : Item, Drop chance, Min quantity, Max quantity . There is a limitation when defining as part of a list(...): filenames can only be used in the first list element.
valuetypes.version: defined as: a string of three numbers, separated by dots (e.g. "1.2.03")
valuetypes.raw: This is plain text, including line breaks. It is used only for map layer data.
valuetypes.stat_id: a string that can be any of the following: A base stat (e.g.  hp  or  avoidance ); A min or max damage type from  engine/damage_types.txt  (e.g.  dmg_melee_min  or  dmg_ment_max ); An elemental resistance from  engine/elements.txt . To use an element as a resistance,  _resist  is appened to the element id (e.g.  fire_resist )
valuetypes.level_scaled_value: a string representing a key/value pair that is delimited by a colon (':'). The first half represents the scaling method, and can be one of the following values:  base ,  player_level ,  item_level , or a primary stat ID. The second half is the value, which is a float. For convenience, it is possible to specify only the value part to define the 'base' value (e.g.  price=10  is the same as  price=base:10 ). Level scaling assumes level 1 is included in the base. So a level 5 item with  price=item_level:1  would equate to 4, not 5. Additionally, the result can be rounded and/or clamped. To round, use  round:true . To set the minimum to, for example, 0, use  min:0 . Likewise,  max:1  would set the maximum to 1.
